_note: Hand-adjudicated overlay of openai/math (fd4aeeb) onto board-finder/playability/ranking_v16.json. ranking_v16.json is ProofAtlas's imported payload and is NOT edited; join on problemId. 'adjudicated' rows carry a status consequence and every one was checked against the family's abstracts and Lean scope note in families.json. 'considered_no_status_effect' rows are the semantic sweep's ADJACENT and NAME_COLLISION pairs, kept so a refresh knows they were looked at; they were NOT individually verified and change nothing. Run apply_ranking_overlay.py to validate and to regenerate ranking_overlay.json.

relations.SAME_TARGET: the family claims to settle the record's exactTarget as stated (proof, disproof, or independence)
relations.SUBCASE: the family claims a named special case, one direction, a weaker form or a parameter range
relations.BOUND_OR_NUMBER: the family claims to improve a bound the record's target or status text names, without settling it

tiers.FORMAL: the family's Lean scope note says the formalized statement is the claim this row relies on
tiers.FORMAL_WEAKER: a formalization exists and proves a weaker form of that claim
tiers.PAPER_ONLY: no formal statement of the claim or of a weaker form of it; a Lean file on a different statement does not count

adjudicated.reason: The record asks that every rational Hodge class on every smooth complex projective variety be algebraic. Family 032 proves the rational Hodge conjecture for every complex CM abelian variety in every dimension and codimension (its further bullets treat abelian and K3 self-powers), a named special class.

The record asks BSD (rank equality and leading-term formula) for every elliptic curve over Q. Family 002 proves the full BSD formula for every E/Q whose full q-power Selmer group has corank zero or one for some prime q, including finiteness of Sha; this is a restricted class of curves over Q.

Family 004 contains a pointwise 2-converse: for E/Q with nonzero rational 2-torsion whose 2-infinity Selmer corank is zero or one, the analytic and Mordell-Weil ranks equal that corank and Sha is finite. This settles BSD rank equality for a subclass of E/Q, not all of them.

Family 006 proves Goldfeld's density statements for quadratic twists of every E/Q (analytic ranks 0 and 1 each have density 1/2; the mean analytic rank tends to 1/2), which are not BSD for any single curve. The summary of family 002 says that combined with 002 they give full BSD for a density-one set of quadratic twists of each E/Q, a subclass of the record.

The record asks surjectivity of the l-adic cycle class map for every smooth projective variety over a finitely generated field. Family 032 states, via Milne's theorems, the Tate conjecture for all abelian varieties over finite fields, a named special case.

The record asks for a total algorithm deciding, for any integer polynomial in any number of variables, whether it has a rational zero. Family 004 proves no such algorithm exists (the number of variables is part of the input), negating the record's claim; the record's STATUS says open, so this conflicts.

The record asks Grothendieck's generalized Hodge statement for every smooth projective complex variety. Family 032 lists the generalized Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties among its consequences, a named special class.

The record asks omega_Q = 2 for tensor rank over Q. Family 107 proves omega(C) <= 9/4 over the complex numbers and omega(F) < 2.371054886 over every field F of any characteristic (including Q), improving the 2.371177 figure in the STATUS but not reaching 2; the complex bound does not transfer to Q by itself.

The record asks that the Anderson model on Z^d (d >= 3) have a regime of absolutely continuous spectrum, equivalently a conducting phase and mobility edge. Family 261 proves purely absolutely continuous spectrum for weak disorder in every fixed d >= 3 with independent uniform site potentials; this covers the uniform model only and does not address the mobility-edge clause.

The record asks, for each eps, delta > 0 with eps + delta < 1, a fixed k for which distinguishing Unique Games value >= 1-eps from value <= delta is NP-hard. Family 102 claims a deterministic reduction from 3SAT to Unique Games over a fixed alphabet with completeness >= 1-eps0 and soundness <= delta0 for all eps0, delta0 in (0,1/2); a stronger gap with eps0 <= eps and delta0 <= delta implies the record's range. The record's STATUS says UGC is open, so this conflicts.

The record asks, for every n >= 4, that a compact set in R^n containing a unit segment in every direction have Hausdorff dimension n. Family 074 proves this for n = 4 (and the 3D Kakeya maximal estimate, which is outside the record's range), so it covers one dimension in the range.

The record asks, for every degree n >= 2, finiteness of limit cycles and their maximal number and configurations. Family 143 proves a uniform bound depending only on the degree (the finiteness part) and an exact maximum of two cycles for quintic Lienard systems; a general maximal number is not claimed. The record's STATUS says no universal bound was established, so this conflicts.

The record asks m_ADM >= sqrt(A/16 pi) for 3D data with DEC and an outermost apparent horizon, with Schwarzschild rigidity. Family 260 proves the enclosing-area spacetime Penrose inequality for one-ended asymptotically flat data in every n >= 3 under DEC, weak future trapping, positive enclosing area and extra decay assumptions, so the hypotheses differ and rigidity needs extra horizon hypotheses.

The record asks for one absolute delta > 0 with L(beta,chi) nonzero for 1-delta/log q < beta < 1 for every primitive quadratic chi of conductor q >= 3. Family 003's bullet 'Uniform exclusion of Landau-Siegel zeros' claims an absolute c > 0 with (1-beta) log q >= c for every real zero beta in (0,1) of every primitive nonprincipal real Dirichlet L-function of conductor q >= 3, which is the same exclusion with delta = c; the record's STATUS still says open, so this conflicts.

The record asks Fontaine-Mazur for every number field, every prime l and every irreducible l-adic representation. Family 010 proves that odd irreducible 2-dimensional 2-adic representations of G_Q, unramified outside finitely many primes and de Rham at 2 with distinct Hodge-Tate weights, are modular up to twist; this is the K = Q, l = 2, dimension-two case.

The record asks, for every number field K and every E/K with End = Z, a GL2-equivariant injection of pi(E) into the cohomology of Thorne's spaces. Family 030 proves that every elliptic curve over every imaginary quadratic field is modular with matching local parameters at every place; this covers imaginary quadratic K, though the family does not state the cohomological injection itself.

The record asks sharp L^p(R^d) to L^q(S^{d-1}) restriction for every d >= 2, including non-endpoint ranges. Family 077 proves the diagonal Fourier extension estimate L^p(Sigma) to L^p(R^3) for positively curved surfaces in R^3 (p > 3) and a bounded-data sphere estimate in R^3, a named d = 3 special case.

The record asks that Sha(E/K) be finite for every elliptic curve over every number field. Family 002 proves Sha finite for E/Q whose full q-power Selmer group has corank zero or one at some prime q, a restricted class over Q.

Family 004's pointwise 2-converse proves Sha finite for E/Q with nonzero rational 2-torsion and 2-infinity Selmer corank zero or one. This is a restricted class of curves over Q, not all E over all number fields.

The record asks that the coefficient-free reduced assembly map K_top(G) to K(C*_r G) be an isomorphism for every second-countable locally compact group. Family 285 disproves rational injectivity of this assembly map for a finitely generated torsion-free group and separately exhibits a K0 class outside its image, so it is not an isomorphism; the record's STATUS says open, so this conflicts.

The record asks that the exact affine determinantal complexity of per_n over C be non-O(n^c) for every c, i.e. superpolynomial. Family 108 proves an Omega(n^3) lower bound on border, and therefore exact, determinantal complexity of the permanent, improving the quadratic bounds the STATUS names but staying polynomial.

The record asks whether every polynomial-time language lies in O(log n) space. The STATUS mentions square-root-space simulation; family 137 improves the square-root exponent for one-tape time simulation to T^{2/5} polylog space, which is still polynomial space and does not reach logarithmic space.

The record asks termination of every (K_X+Delta)-flip sequence for lc or klt pairs in every dimension. Family 056 proves termination of generalized log canonical flip sequences on compact Kahler fourfolds and of permitted MMPs for projective lc fourfolds with rational boundary, a dimension-four case with extra hypotheses.

The record asks that K_X+Delta be semiample for every minimal projective klt pair. Family 034 claims log abundance in every dimension over algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero: a nef Q-Cartier log canonical adjoint on a projective lc pair with effective rational boundary is semiample. This settles the record if Delta is the usual effective Q-divisor, which the record does not state; the record's STATUS says open, so this conflicts.

The record asks Chowla correlation sums o(x) for every k >= 2 tuple of shifts with nonproportional affine forms. Family 007 proves the ordinary two-point case k = 2 with an O(X/(log X)^c) bound, a named special case.

The record asks whether every simple graph with no K_{t+1} minor is t-colourable, i.e. chi(G) <= h(G). Family 157 constructs arbitrarily large graphs with independence number at most two and chi(G) > h(G) (even fractional chi_f > h), a counterexample to the stated conjecture; the record's STATUS says ordinary Hadwiger remains open, so this conflicts.

The record asks finiteness of maximal atypical subvarieties for mixed Shimura varieties. Family 016 proves the abelian (pure Shimura) Zilber-Pink conjecture over Q-bar and the Hodge-generic curve case in A_2, a pure-Shimura special case; the record's STATUS notes that pure-Shimura cases do not cover the target.

The record asks non-zero off-diagonal long-range order at low temperature in the thermodynamic limit for an interacting continuous 3D Bose gas. Family 267 proves positive-temperature condensation for the dilute hard-sphere gas at small density, and a density-uniform bound for bounded nonnegative radial finite-range interactions at temperatures up to the square of the density; this covers named interaction classes and regimes.

The record asks numerical primitive positivity (the standard conjecture of Hodge type) for every smooth projective variety. Family 032 proves the Hodge standard conjecture for abelian varieties in arbitrary characteristic, a special class of varieties.

The record asks S(rho_A) <= C |boundary A| for unique ground states of finite-range 2D square-lattice Hamiltonians with fixed local dimension and a size-independent gap lower bound. Family 265 proves an entropy area law for unique ground states of finite-range Hamiltonians on any finite induced square-lattice domain, using only a uniform full-system gap and local bounds; the record's STATUS says open, so this conflicts.

The record asks Grothendieck's section conjecture for every hyperbolic genus >= 2 curve over every number field. Family 019 proves the global statement over number fields only when the finite-cover descent locus equals the rational points, which includes X_0(N) and X_1(N) of genus >= 2 over Q; its main theorem is the local p-adic case.

Record asks that every rational Hodge class on every smooth projective complex variety be absolute Hodge. Family 032 proves the rational Hodge conjecture for every complex CM abelian variety; algebraic classes are absolute Hodge, so absolute Hodge holds on CM abelian varieties, a named special case (the record already lists abelian varieties as established).

Record asks for a positive gap for every integer spin S>=1 and gaplessness for every half-integer spin. Family 268 proves a uniform positive spectral gap for the pure antiferromagnetic spin-one Heisenberg chain on even periodic rings, which is the S=1 gapped case only; other integer spins and the gapless half-integer claim are not addressed.

Record asks kappa(X) >= kappa(Y)+kappa(F) for a surjective morphism of smooth projective varieties with general fibre F (Iitaka C_{n,m}). Family 033's 'Projective Hodge lines and ordinary Iitaka subadditivity' proves kappa(X) >= kappa(F)+kappa(Z) for surjective projective morphisms between smooth connected projective varieties over algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero; it assumes connected fibres, the standard normalization the record leaves implicit.

Record asks whether every homotopy equivalence between closed aspherical manifolds is homotopic to a homeomorphism (Borel conjecture). Family 320 constructs closed aspherical topological four-manifolds that are homotopy equivalent but not homeomorphic, so the homotopy equivalence between them cannot be homotopic to a homeomorphism; this disproves the target in the topological category used by the record's homeomorphism wording.

Record asks for a polynomial bound K <= d^q on the number of limit cycles of planar degree-d polynomial systems. Family 143 proves the weaker uniform boundedness: the number of limit cycles is bounded by a finite constant depending only on d (second part of Hilbert's sixteenth problem), with no polynomial rate; the exact count of two cycles for quintic Lienard systems is a special case.

Record asks that no closed aspherical manifold admits a metric of positive scalar curvature (Gromov-Lawson aspherical conjecture). Family 335's manuscript 'Positive scalar curvature forces rational inessentiality' proves that closed manifolds with PSC are rationally inessential with no spin or fundamental-group hypothesis, and the family states this proves the Gromov-Lawson aspherical conjecture, since closed aspherical manifolds are rationally essential.

Record asks N(sigma,T) <= C T^{2(1-sigma)+eps} for 1/2 <= sigma <= 1. Family 003 proves zeta and all Dirichlet L-functions have no zeros in Re s > 7/8; for sigma in (7/8,1] this forces N(sigma,T)=0 for large T, so the density bound holds on that range, and nothing is claimed for sigma <= 7/8.

Record asks whether every A in N with divergent reciprocal sum must contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions (Erdos problem 3). Family 159 proves Erdos's conjecture that every set of positive integers with divergent reciprocal sum contains progressions of every finite length, which is the same statement.

Record asks whether every hyperbolic group with boundary S^2 acts properly, cocompactly and isometrically on H^3 (equivalently is virtually a cocompact Kleinian group). Family 246 proves that every hyperbolic group with boundary S^2 admits a proper cocompact isometric action on H^3 with finite kernel, which gives the virtual form and proves Cannon's conjecture.

Record asks whether every nonidentity element of every word-hyperbolic group is detected by a homomorphism to a finite group (residual finiteness). Family 252 constructs a torsion-free word-hyperbolic group that is not residually finite, so some nonidentity element is not separated by finite quotients, which refutes the statement.

Record asks whether every language decided by a bounded-error probabilistic logspace polynomial-time machine is decided deterministically in O(log n) space. Family 103 proves L = RL = BPL with an effective compiler, which is that equality of classes.

Record asks for periodic Reeb orbits of every contact form on every closed contact manifold. Family 345 proves infinitely many prime closed geodesics on every Riemannian S^n and on every closed 3-manifold; geodesic flows are Reeb flows of the canonical contact form on unit cotangent bundles, so periodic Reeb orbits are established for those contact manifolds and forms only, a named special case.

Record asks the sharp Bochner-Riesz characterization in every dimension d>=2 for 1<p<infinity. Family 078 proves boundedness of the Bochner-Riesz multipliers on R^3 for delta > max{3|1/p-1/2|-1/2, 0}, which is the strict range in dimension three only, with no endpoint and no other dimensions.

Record asks that every Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of a closed connected symplectic manifold has at least Crit(M) fixed points. Family 347 constructs a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of the complex quadric threefold with exactly three fixed points, at least one degenerate, while every smooth function on it has at least four critical points; this disproves the critical-number form as stated.

Record asks whether L(F_m) and L(F_n) are isomorphic for m != n, especially L(F_2) = L(F_3). Family 287 proves L(F_2) and L(F_3) are isomorphic as tracial von Neumann algebras, hence all interpolated free group factors including L(F_infinity) are isomorphic, which answers the record affirmatively.

Record asks whether equal Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps of two smooth metrics on a compact connected manifold of dimension n>=3 with boundary force the metrics to differ by a diffeomorphism fixing the boundary pointwise. Family 365 proves a smooth Riemannian metric is determined, up to a diffeomorphism fixing the measured patch, by its zero-frequency Dirichlet-to-Neumann energy form on any nonempty open boundary patch; with the whole boundary as the patch this gives the record's conclusion.

Polyakov's conjecture: exponential decay of O(n) two-point functions on Z^2 for n >= 3 at every beta. Family 215 claims exactly this at every positive temperature. FORMAL_WEAKER: the Lean statement gives uniform exponential decay on every finite square-lattice subgraph with free boundary and couplings at most beta; the infinite-volume statement is the limit of those uniform bounds but is not itself stated.

Record asks for the order of magnitude of r_3(N), the largest 3-AP-free subset of {1..N}, whose status cites the current upper bound N exp(-c (log N)^{1/6}/log log N). Family 159 proves r_k(N) <= C_k N exp(-c_k (log N)^{eps_k}) for every k>=3, including k=3; the exponent eps_3 is not stated in the digest, so whether it improves the cited bound cannot be verified from the record.

Record asks that the exploration path of critical FK models with q<=4 converges to SLE_{kappa(q)} with conformal invariance as mesh tends to zero. Family 223 proves chordal SLE_kappa convergence of critical square-lattice FK Dobrushin interfaces for 0<q<=4 with kappa=4pi/arccos(-sqrt(q)/2), for all bounded Jordan domains when q>=1 but only smooth Jordan domains when q<1, under marked-boundary approximations; this is a square-lattice, restricted-domain subcase.

Record asks kappa(K_X+Delta) >= 0 for projective lc pairs with pseudo-effective K_X+Delta (nonvanishing). Family 034's 'Log abundance in characteristic zero' manuscript proves canonical nonvanishing for smooth projective varieties over C in every dimension, which is the Delta=0 smooth case; general boundaries and singular lc pairs are not covered.

Record asks w(E/K) = (-1)^rank for every elliptic curve over every number field. Family 002 proves full BSD for E/Q whose q-Selmer corank is 0 or 1 for some prime q, giving analytic rank = Mordell-Weil rank there and hence the root-number parity for those curves over Q; this is a named subcase (E/Q with low corank), not all number fields.

Record asks for global classical solutions for every sufficiently regular finite-energy initial datum. Family 362 proves global existence and uniqueness for arbitrary smooth admissible data whose initial particle density is compactly supported and whose fields have finite energy and bounded derivatives; compact support of the density is a restriction on the data class.

Record asks that every integer a other than -1 that is not a square is a primitive root for a positive natural density of primes, with Artin's correction factor. Family 029 proves the infinitude: at least c_a x/(log x)^2 primes in (x,2x) have primitive root a for every such a, a weaker form without positive density or the Artin constant.

Record asks, for every d>=2 and compact E in R^d with Hausdorff dimension greater than d/2, that the distance set has positive one-dimensional Lebesgue measure. Family 073 resolves the Falconer distance conjecture in every dimension d>=2 with this hypothesis and conclusion.

Record asks that every closed even-dimensional manifold with positive sectional curvature has positive Euler characteristic (Hopf). Family 348 classifies closed Einstein four-manifolds with positive Einstein constant and nonnegative sectional curvature; their universal covers (S^4, CP^2, S^2 x S^2, and RP^4 in the strictly positive case) give positive Euler characteristic, so this is the Einstein four-dimensional subcase.

Record asks the wave local smoothing estimate for every n>=3 and p>2n/(n-1) with loss s_p-1/p+eps. Family 079 proves the local smoothing estimate in three spatial dimensions for 2<p<infinity with regularity above max{0,1-3/p}, which for n=3 and p>3 is exactly the record's regularity; dimensions n>=4 are not covered.

Record asks that every locally compact group acting faithfully on a connected manifold is a Lie group, equivalently that Z_p has no faithful action on a connected manifold. Family 304 proves this in every finite dimension for second-countable Hausdorff groups acting jointly continuously on manifolds without boundary; Z_p is covered directly, so the record's equivalent Z_p form is settled, and second countability is the only extra restriction.

Record asks for a translation-invariant zero-field Gibbs state with nonzero spin expectation for the nearest-neighbour isotropic quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet on Z^d, for every d>=3 and every spin S, at all sufficiently low beta. Family 271 proves, for every d>=3 and S, a translation-invariant spontaneously magnetized KMS equilibrium state at every sufficiently low positive temperature with magnetization at least S/4.

Record asks whether K[G] is a domain for every torsion-free group G and every field K. Family 196 constructs a finitely presented torsion-free group G with nonzero alpha, beta in F2[G] and alpha*beta = 0, a counterexample for K = F2.

Record asks that every bounded entire monotone solution of Allen-Cahn is one-dimensional for each dimension 4<=N<=8. Family 375 proves the N=8 case (every entire solution on R^8 with positive directional derivative is a planar heteroclinic) and classifies stable solutions on R^7; strictly monotone solutions are stable, so N=7 also follows (my inference, not stated by the family), but N=4,5,6 are not covered.

Record asks the exact limiting threshold r_3 of uniform random 3-SAT. Family 235 proves that a finite positive limiting satisfiability threshold exists for every k>=3 (the existence component) and that the 3-SAT threshold is a computable real with explicit certificates, but does not identify r_3; its model samples clauses on distinct variables with replacement rather than the record's distinct-literal uniform model.

Record asks, for every n>=3 and every finitely presented integral Poincare duality group of dimension n, a closed aspherical n-manifold realizing it (Wall's conjecture). Family 305 constructs a finitely presented integral PD4 group with finite classifying space that is not the fundamental group of any closed aspherical topological four-manifold, refuting the claim at n=4.

Record asks whether every bounded representation of a C*-algebra on a Hilbert space is similar to a *-representation. Family 288 proves Kadison's similarity conjecture: every bounded unital homomorphism from a unital complex C*-algebra into bounded operators on any Hilbert space is similar to a *-homomorphism; the non-unital reduction is not spelled out in the family.

Record asks the exact chromatic number of the plane (Hadwiger-Nelson). Family 158 proves that every five-colouring of the plane has a monochromatic unit-distance pair, so the chromatic number is 6 or 7; this improves the lower bound from 5 but does not determine the number.

Record asks the descendant Virasoro constraints for every smooth projective complex variety X. Family 065 proves the full descendant Virasoro conjecture for smooth complete intersections in projective space (all genera, curve classes and insertions) and transfers it to projectivizations of vector bundles over such bases, so only these varieties are covered.

Record asks that L2-Betti numbers of every closed aspherical n-manifold vanish outside degree n/2 for all n, in particular odd n. Family 315 proves the four-dimensional case (finite aspherical integral Poincare complexes of formal dimension four are included), a single dimension of the general conjecture.

Record asks that the Salvetti complex of every Coxeter system with finite S and arbitrary labels be aspherical (Artin K(pi,1)). Family 254 proves that the standard Salvetti complex of every Artin group with finitely many standard generators is aspherical, the same statement.

Record asks that the lower energy per particle of any completely monotone potential p(r)=f(r^2), infinite values allowed, is at least the hexagonal-lattice energy at density one. Family 090 proves the density-one triangular lattice minimizes the lower energy per particle for every nonnegative completely monotone function of squared distance among planar configurations of centred-disk density one, with infinite energies included.
Record asks whether RL = L for the stated read-only-input, log-space RL model. Family 103 proves L = RL = BPL, which contains RL = L.

Record asserts that every group is good in the four-dimensional disc-embedding sense, equivalently that F2 is good. Family 305 proves that the unrestricted disc-embedding statement fails and that F2, and any group containing it, is not good in the Freedman-Quinn sense.

Record asks holomorphic convexity of the universal cover of every connected smooth complex projective variety. Family 046 states a separate smooth connected projective complex surface whose universal cover is not holomorphically convex, disproving the unrestricted conjecture in dimension two (its fourfold has large fundamental group and non-Stein universal cover).

Record asks t(H,W) >= t(K2,W)^{|E(H)|} for every bipartite H and every graphon W. Family 161 exhibits one connected bipartite graph on 35 vertices and 66 edges and a finite host graph (hence a graphon) with t(H,G) < t(K2,G)^66, a counterexample.

Record asks the bound H^{n-1}({phi=0}) <= C sqrt(lambda) for every closed Riemannian n-manifold with n>=2. Family 350 proves it for surfaces, but constructs smooth metrics on S^3 arbitrarily close to round and on S^2 x T^2 with unbounded nodal measure over sqrt(lambda), and power-law violations on S^4 x S^1, so the universal claim fails in dimensions three and four.

Family 337 claims the generalized Cartan-Hadamard isoperimetric inequality in every dimension with Euclidean-ball equality rigidity for kappa = 0. FORMAL_WEAKER: the Lean statement is the sharp Euclidean FILLING inequality for integral n-cycles in proper CAT(0) spaces, which gives the inequality for regions (in a Cartan-Hadamard manifold the region is the filling of its boundary) but not the equality rigidity. CAUTION carried from this repository's own record: an earlier human settlement claim on this target was withdrawn.

Record asserts that every closed exact Lagrangian in T^*N is Hamiltonian isotopic to the zero section N. Family 340 constructs, in T^*(S^9 x S^{N-1}) for some large even N, a closed exact embedded Lagrangian diffeomorphic to the base but not Hamiltonian isotopic to the zero section.

Record asks |K||K°| >= 4^n/n! for centrally symmetric convex bodies with equality at the cube. Family 087 proves the symmetric Mahler conjecture in every dimension with equality exactly for invertible linear images of Hanner polytopes, which include the cube and its polar.

MISSED BY THE SEMANTIC SWEEP, recovered by the lexical recall screen. Kuznetsov: a smooth cubic fourfold is rational iff Ku(X) ~= D^b(S) for a K3 surface S. Family 054 claims, for every sufficiently large admissible Hassett discriminant, a very general cubic fourfold that is IRRATIONAL although its Kuznetsov component is equivalent to D^b of a projective K3 -- refuting the 'if' direction. Ineffective threshold; paper only.

Record asks whether every bipartite entangled state has strictly positive distillable secret key under asymptotic LOCC with public communication. Family 272 constructs an entangled state on C^10 x C^10 with zero distillable secret key for protocols that process all copies jointly with unlimited two-way public communication and an eavesdropper holding the purification, a counterexample.

The record is universal over fields of every characteristic and torsion-free G. If ab = 1 and ba != 1 in K[G], then e = ba is idempotent ((ba)(ba) = b(ab)a = ba), e != 1 by hypothesis, and e != 0 since a = (ab)a = a(ba). So family 197's October-4 manuscript -- a finitely presented TORSION-FREE group with F_2[G] not directly finite -- would give a nontrivial idempotent in F_2[G]. PAPER_ONLY: the formalized direct-finiteness counterexample is for a group WITH torsion (odd prime order), which does not touch this record. Read with family 207 (SUBCASE, FORMAL): the characteristic-zero half is claimed proved. Net claimed state: true in characteristic 0, false in characteristic 2.

Record asks that every idempotent of K[G] is 0 or 1 for every field K of any characteristic and every torsion-free G. Family 207 proves this for every torsion-free group and every commutative unital characteristic-zero domain (so all characteristic-zero fields), leaving positive characteristic open.

Record asserts C_DFT(n) >= c n log n for all large n in the model where each step forms lambda f + mu g. Family 130's later version gives exact DFT circuits of size o(n log n) along an unbounded sequence of lengths, counting every addition, subtraction and scalar multiplication, which refutes the uniform lower bound.

Record asks a smooth strictly Griffiths-positive Hermitian metric on every ample holomorphic vector bundle. Family 050 constructs ample rank-two bundles on P^1 x P^1 (coordinatewise power pullbacks tensored with O(1,1)) that admit no such metric for all sufficiently large powers, a counterexample.

Record asks that each p-block B of a finite group has as many simple modules as there are G-conjugacy classes of B-weights. Family 202 proves the numerical blockwise Alperin weight conjecture for every prime and finite group: the number of irreducible Brauer characters in a block equals the number of conjugacy classes of its weights.

Record asks that a smooth strictly convex positive-curvature planar billiard whose grazing annulus is foliated by continuous T-invariant essential curves be an ellipse, circles included. Family 147 proves that a continuous foliation of a full grazing annulus by individually invariant essential curves forces the boundary to be an ellipse, which is the invariant-curve formulation the record selects.

Record asks whether every finitely presented group in which every element has finite order is finite. Family 247 constructs an infinite finitely presented periodic group (every element of finite order), so the statement fails.

Record asks whether S^2 x S^2 admits a metric of positive sectional curvature (Hopf). Family 348 classifies closed Einstein four-manifolds with positive sectional curvature (up to scaling S^4, CP^2, RP^4), which excludes S^2 x S^2 among Einstein metrics; it says nothing about non-Einstein metrics, so it is a special case only.
Record asks whether Thompson's group F of dyadic piecewise-linear homeomorphisms of [0,1] is amenable. Family 248 proves F is nonamenable, which answers the question negatively.

Record asks for a positive-Lebesgue-measure set of parameters k at which f_k(x,y)=(x+y+k sin 2pi x, y+k sin 2pi x) mod Z^2 has positive metric entropy. Family 146 proves positive metric entropy for the standard sine map at every sufficiently large parameter, a full tail that contains such a positive-measure set.

Record asks whether ambient topological equivalence of reduced hypersurface germs in C^n forces equal multiplicity. Family 059 constructs ambiently homeomorphic reduced hypersurface germs of multiplicities 2 and 3 (in a space of dimension divisible by 8) and of multiplicities 4 and 5 in C^4, which refutes the universal statement.

Record asks for |(1-lambda)K +_0 lambda L| >= |K|^(1-lambda) |L|^lambda for origin-symmetric convex bodies K, L and lambda in [0,1]. Family 091 proves the logarithmic Brunn-Minkowski inequality for arbitrary origin-symmetric convex bodies in every dimension.

Record asks whether equal full weak Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps of bounded measurable real scalar conductivities (uniformly positive and bounded) on bounded connected Lipschitz domains in every R^n, n>=3, force equal conductivities. Family 365 (bullet dated 23 Sep 2026) constructs two distinct uniformly positive bounded measurable conductivities on a ball in R^3 with the same full DN operator, a counterexample at n=3; the record's status calls this endpoint open, so the family's date is a point for the reviewer to check.

Record asks that every nonempty connected open domain of the Riemann sphere be conformally homeomorphic to a circle domain (complementary components round disks or points). Family 071 proves that every domain in the Riemann sphere is conformally equivalent to a circle domain, resolving Koebe's conjecture positively.

Record asks for p_c < p_u if and only if the group is nonamenable, for Cayley graphs of finitely generated infinite groups. Family 214 proves only the 'if' direction (nonamenable quasi-transitive graphs have p_c < p_u); the converse (amenable implies p_c = p_u) is not claimed.

Record asks that every plane curve of degree d with multiplicities at least m_i at r >= 10 very general points satisfy d > (1/sqrt r) sum m_i. Family 039 proves the equivalent strict inequality sum m_i < d sqrt(r) for every nonzero effective plane curve through r >= 10 very general points, with arbitrary multiplicities.

Record asks that K_X+(n+1)L be basepoint-free for smooth projective X of dimension n and ample L. Family 038 proves Fujita's freeness conjecture: K_X+mL is globally generated for every m >= n+1, which implies basepoint-freeness.
