Record asks NP-hardness of MCSP, the circuit-size problem for truth tables. Family 112 gives 2^{omega(sqrt n)} gate lower bounds for an explicit polynomial-time language in depth-three circuits; same circuit-size theme but no hardness reduction for MCSP.

Record asks for a polynomial simplex pivot rule. Family 104 gives quasipolynomial deterministic algorithms for mean-payoff, stochastic and parity games; strategy-improvement and pivoting methods are related, but no simplex pivot rule is constructed.

Family 002 gives full BSD for E/Q with low Selmer corank, which covers some congruent-number curves (quadratic twists of y^2 = x^3 - x) and identifies rank with analytic rank there, but gives no classification of all congruent n.

Record asks which integers are congruent numbers, i.e. which twists E_n: y^2 = x^3 - n^2 x of y^2 = x^3 - x have positive rank. Family 006 proves density statements for analytic ranks among quadratic twists of every E/Q, which concern these twist families statistically but do not classify congruent n.

Family 257 constructs a word-hyperbolic group with a finite aspherical complex and no geometric action on any proper complete CAT(0) space; same class of hyperbolic groups and geometric-action question, but a different target space and no H^3 result.

Record asks superlinear gate lower bounds for explicit functions in unrestricted-depth fan-in-two circuits. Family 112 gives 2^{omega(sqrt n)} lower bounds for depth-three unbounded fan-in OR-AND-OR circuits, a restricted model with no implication for fan-in-two circuits.

Record concerns global periods of automorphic representations and nonvanishing of L(pi,R,1/2) (Gan-Gross-Prasad). Family 014 proves Arthur enhancements and Ramanujan-type temperedness for cuspidal representations over global function fields; same automorphic-period and Arthur setting, but no GGP equivalence.

Record asks a uniform bound on torsion points of abelian varieties of dimension at least two over number fields. Family 016 proves the abelian Zilber-Pink conjecture over Qbar (finiteness of maximal atypical subvarieties), a Manin-Mumford-type finiteness result on abelian varieties, but no uniform torsion bound.
Family 257 gives a word-hyperbolic group without a geometric CAT(0) action, another structural failure for hyperbolic groups; same group class but a different property.

Record asks uniform bounds c(g,F) on rational points of genus-g curves over number fields. Family 019 proves the local p-adic section conjecture for genus at least two and section-conjecture consequences for X_0(N) and X_1(N); these are rational-point results in the nonabelian section approach, not uniform boundedness.

Record asks whether no-slip Leray-Hopf solutions converge to the Euler solution as viscosity tends to zero. Family 376 constructs forced incompressible Navier-Stokes flows at each fixed positive computable viscosity; it concerns viscous forced flows and has no vanishing-viscosity limit.

Record asks equidistribution of Frobenius classes in the Sato-Tate group for higher-dimensional abelian varieties. Family 032 proves the rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties and, via Milne, the Tate conjecture over finite fields; Hodge-theoretic input relevant to Sato-Tate groups, but no equidistribution.

Record asks uniform subconvexity |L(1/2,pi)| <= A C(pi)^{1/4-delta} for GL(n) over number fields. Family 014 proves Ramanujan at places and Arthur-type decompositions over global function fields; temperedness of local components is a neighbouring automorphic bound, not a subconvexity exponent over number fields.

Record asks whether NP = existential theory of the reals. Family 141 proves that the existential theory of the reals lies in the counting hierarchy, an upper complexity bound that does not decide NP versus the existential theory of the reals.

Record asks limsup (p_{n+1}-p_n)/(log p_n)^2 = 1 (Cramer). Family 026 proves that for each C>0 a positive proportion of prime gaps exceed C log p_n; this is a log-scale large-gap result, far from the (log p)^2 scale and the limsup.

Record asks whether every group is hyperlinear (approximate unitary representations in normalized Hilbert-Schmidt norm). Family 251 proves amenability is equivalent to unitarizability and to strong Ulam stability in operator norm; these are amenable-side approximate-representation results, not hyperlinearity of arbitrary groups.

Family 121 gives an almost-linear randomized (1+eps)-approximation for edit distance in word-RAM time N^{1+o(1)}; a fine-grained algorithmic result in the same randomized word-RAM setting, with no 3SUM content.

Record asks for no Las Vegas word-RAM 3SUM algorithm in worst-case expected O(n^{2-eps}) time. Family 138 gives a randomized word-RAM algorithm for Subset Sum in O(2^{0.49n}) time; a sum-type problem in the same randomized word-RAM model, but a different problem and bound.

Record asks whether no nonzero polynomial P in Q[X,Y] satisfies P(e,pi)=0. Family 017 proves the irrationality exponent of pi is exactly 2, a Diophantine-approximation result about pi alone that does not address algebraic independence of e and pi.

Record asks whether every smooth S^3 in S^4 is smoothly unknotted (smooth Schoenflies). Family 305 disproves the unrestricted topological four-dimensional disk-embedding conjecture and Wall's realization conjecture; same four-dimensional topology area, but about locally flat topological disks, not smooth Schoenflies.

Record asks that a global horizontal section of the Gauss-Manin bundle algebraic at one fibre is algebraic at all fibres. Family 001 proves Milne's rationality for specialized Hodge classes of abelian varieties with good reduction, a specialization statement about Hodge classes but not the variational one.

Family 032 proves the rational Hodge conjecture on each complex CM abelian variety, a single-fibre statement; algebraic classes on fibres are the input to variational statements, but the family says nothing about how classes vary in families.

Record asks whether x2 and x3 invariant ergodic measures are Lebesgue or finitely supported (Furstenberg). Family 148 proves that the Hausdorff dimension of a finite real self-similar measure equals min{1, h_RW/chi}, the dimension-entropy framework used in invariant-measure questions, but does not treat x2x3-invariance.

Record asks whether the subtour LP integrality gap for metric TSP equals 4/3. Family 117 proves NP-hardness of Uniform Sparsest Cut and Goemans-Linial SDP integrality gaps of order sqrt(log n)/(log log n)^3; same integrality-gap methodology for relaxations, with no TSP or 4/3 content.

Family 339 proves Katok's entropy rigidity for geodesic flows of closed negatively curved manifolds; geodesic flows are Reeb flows on unit cotangent bundles, but the family concerns entropy maximization rather than periodic orbits.

Family 077 proves the diagonal Fourier extension conjecture for positively curved surfaces in R^3 (L^p bounds for p>3); a neighbouring Fourier-restriction result used alongside Bochner-Riesz-type estimates, but not the Bochner-Riesz claim.

Record asks whether P_R differs from NP_R in the Blum-Shub-Smale real model. Family 141 places the existential theory of the reals in the counting hierarchy, a complexity statement about real-number computation that does not separate P_R from NP_R.

Record asks equivalences (L-space, left-orderable pi_1, taut foliation) for rational homology spheres. Family 306 proves the purely cosmetic surgery conjecture for nontrivial knots in S^3; Dehn surgery is common to both, but no Heegaard Floer or foliation statement is made.

Record asks zeta'(rho) != 0 for every nontrivial zero (simplicity). Family 003 proves a zero-free half-plane Re s > 7/8 for Dirichlet L-functions, which locates zeros but says nothing about their multiplicities.

Record asks Murre's Chow-Kunneth package (A)-(D) for all smooth projective varieties. Family 040 proves Bloch's conjecture for complex surfaces with p_g = 0 (Albanese isomorphism on degree-zero zero-cycles), a surface-case input in the Murre circle, not the package itself.

Record asks a polynomial-time quantum algorithm for hidden subgroups of S_n. Family 279 gives an exact probability-one quantum factoring circuit family over a fixed gate set; factoring is the abelian hidden-subgroup case, but no non-abelian hidden-subgroup algorithm is given.

Record asks global continuation of classical solutions to the inhomogeneous Landau-Coulomb equation. Family 363 proves nonuniqueness for the periodic hard-sphere Boltzmann equation with local conservation; Landau-type equations arise from grazing Boltzmann-type collisions, but the equation and question differ.
Family 003's Landau-Siegel zero exclusion shares the name Landau with the Landau-Coulomb equation, but concerns real zeros of Dirichlet L-functions and has no kinetic-equation content.

Record asks vanishing of rational motivic cohomology H^{n,i}(X) for n <= 0 (Beilinson-Soule). Family 009 reconstructs function fields from mod-l Milnor K-theory and Galois data; it uses K-theory of fields but makes no vanishing claim.

Record asks soliton resolution for the focusing energy-critical wave equation without radial symmetry. Family 079 proves local smoothing for the linear three-dimensional wave equation, a dispersive estimate used in such analyses, but makes no nonlinear resolution statement.

Family 153 classifies singular Bernoulli convolutions via explicit algebraic units and proves singularity at reciprocals of quartic Salem numbers; Salem numbers and small algebraic units are objects in Lehmer's problem, but no Mahler-measure gap is addressed.

Record asks Lehmer's gap for Mahler measures of monic integer polynomials. Family 087 proves the Mahler conjectures on volume products of convex bodies, a different problem that shares Mahler's name and has no Mahler-measure content.

Record asks consistency of ZFR (Reinhardt cardinals without choice). Family 244 proves relative consistency of ZF with the Partition Principle and not Choice; a choice-free ZF independence result in the same model-theoretic area, not Reinhardt cardinals.

Record asks Voevodsky's smash-nilpotence for rational cycles. Family 040 proves Bloch's conjecture for p_g = 0 surfaces (zero-cycles), which relates to nilpotence of degree-zero zero-cycles on such surfaces, but does not address smash-nilpotence in general.

Record asks whether there are infinitely many primes of the form n^2+1. Family 020 proves positive-density power-free values of irreducible polynomials of degree at least four under local conditions, a sieve result on polynomial values rather than prime values of a quadratic.
Record asks transcendence of zeta(3). Family 005 proves Catalan's constant is irrational, an irrationality result for a different constant with no transcendence content.

Family 372 proves global uniqueness of smooth Lame moduli from full static displacement-to-traction data in R^3, a Calderon-type full-data result for isotropic elasticity rather than the Laplace-Beltrami problem.

Family 216 analyses the square-lattice XY (O(2)) model at its BKT transition, with critical correlations and an essential singularity; the O(2) case is the one excluded by the n>=3 hypothesis in Polyakov's conjecture, so it is a contrasting phase transition rather than the claim.

Family 160 proves superexponential lower bounds for van der Waerden numbers (monochromatic k-term progressions in colourings), a related progression-extremal problem but not the size of 3-AP-free sets.
Family 211 proves critical FK planar maps converge to LQG spheres or the Brownian CRT (a geometric phase diagram), about random planar maps rather than convergence of lattice interfaces.

Family 224 proves Cardy's formula for critical Poisson-Voronoi percolation and quenched near-critical universality; critical crossing results on a different random graph, with no FK exploration convergence.

Family 233 proves the joint scaling limit of critical Ashkin-Teller heights and current clusters, including the four-state Potts endpoint; a related critical random-cluster scaling limit, but not the SLE exploration convergence.

Record asks Omega(n log n) lower bounds for Boolean circuits computing integer multiplication. Family 109 gives a deterministic O(n(log n)^{1-kappa}) multiplication algorithm on one Turing machine with finitely many one-dimensional tapes, refuting the Schonhage-Strassen optimality conjecture in that model; it is a different model and gives no circuit lower bound.

Family 130 gives exact Fourier-transform circuits of size o(n log n) along subsequences of lengths, refuting an Omega(n log n) lower bound in the unrestricted complex linear-circuit model; the same n log n circuit-optimality theme, but a linear-algebraic model rather than Boolean multiplication circuits.

Family 035 proves log abundance for projective lc threefolds of numerical dimension one in characteristic p > 3, a restricted abundance statement in the same area as the record's nonvanishing conjecture.

Family 036 proves minimal models for generalized lc pairs with pseudo-effective adjoint and numerical semiampleness of nef adjoints; these are inputs in the MMP-and-abundance route to nonvanishing, but nonvanishing itself is not stated.
Family 056 proves termination of flips for projective and Kahler fourfold minimal model programs, part of the program in which nonvanishing is proved; it does not state nonvanishing.

Family 006's low-corank 2-converse gives the same analytic-equals-Mordell-Weil conclusion for E/Q with 2-Selmer corank at most one, already inside family 002's corank range; its main content is Goldfeld's density conjecture.
Family 274 'Parity is not in QAC0' concerns the parity Boolean function for constant-depth quantum circuits and shares only the word parity with the root-number parity conjecture.
Family 254 concerns Artin groups (Salvetti complexes and K(pi,1)), sharing only the name Artin with Artin's primitive root conjecture.
Family 042 concerns Oka classification of minimal complex surfaces and Hopf surfaces of class VII, sharing only the name Hopf with Hopf's Euler-characteristic conjecture.
Family 080 proves almost-everywhere convergence of Schrodinger evolutions at the sharp Sobolev endpoint (Carleson problem); a related dispersive pointwise problem, not local smoothing.

Family 209 disproves integral Gersten injectivity in K_3 and K_5 for ramified regular local rings of mixed characteristic (0,5); a purity statement in the same circle as the Grothendieck-Serre H^1 injectivity, but with different invariants and no torsor claim.

Family 193 concerns positivity of Serre's intersection multiplicity over regular local rings; it shares Serre's name and the regular-local-ring setting with the Grothendieck-Serre torsor conjecture but is a different statement.
Family 312 concerns Grothendieck's homotopy hypothesis for infinity-groupoids, sharing only the Grothendieck name with the Grothendieck-Serre torsor conjecture.

Record asks Kimura-O'Sullivan finite-dimensionality for all smooth projective varieties. Family 040 proves Bloch's conjecture for p_g = 0 complex surfaces, a surface-case input in the finite-dimensionality literature, but does not prove finite-dimensionality of any motive.
Record is Zauner's conjecture on SIC-POVMs in every dimension. Family 266 resolves Zauner's dimension-six mutually unbiased bases conjecture (N(6)=3), a different problem about MUBs rather than SICs.

Tempting collision: family 084 resolves the geometric-progression case of the Erdos similarity conjecture (large subsets of [0,1] avoiding affine copies of q^n). It has nothing to do with Kadison's similarity problem for C*-algebras.

Tempting collision: family 285 disproves the Kadison-Kaplansky projection conjecture for reduced group C*-algebras of torsion-free groups. Record 280 explicitly excludes operator-algebraic idempotents, so the family does not address its group-ring statement.
Tempting collision: family 294 disproves Kaplansky's quasitrace conjecture (2-quasitraces on C*-algebras), a different Kaplansky conjecture from the idempotent conjecture of record 280.
Tempting collision: family 310 proves Quillen's conjecture on p-subgroup posets (group homology), a different conjecture from the Bass-Quillen question on projective modules over polynomial rings.
Tempting collision: family 321 disproves Wall's finite D(2) problem (finiteness of D(2) complexes), a different Wall problem from Wall's Poincare duality group realization conjecture.

Tempting collision: family 143 addresses Hilbert's sixteenth problem (limit cycles of planar polynomial vector fields), a different Hilbert problem from the resolvent degree of the general degree-seven polynomial.
Tempting collision: family 157 disproves Hadwiger's conjecture (chromatic number versus clique-minor order) for graphs, not the chromatic number of the plane.

Family 197 disproves Kaplansky's direct-finiteness conjecture (ab=1 but ba!=1 in F2[G] for a finitely presented torsion-free G) and does not state a zero-divisor claim. The implication is immediate: e=ba is an idempotent with e and 1-e nonzero, so e(1-e)=0 gives zero divisors and the family also refutes record 202 for K=F2 (reviewer to confirm).

Record concerns long-range order in the d>=3 quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet. Family 268 proves a uniform spectral gap for the spin-one antiferromagnetic Heisenberg chain on even rings, a one-dimensional antiferromagnetic gap result that does not bear on the ferromagnetic ordering question.

Record asks an effective bound Q for rational approximations of real algebraic irrationals (effective Roth). Family 017 proves that the irrationality exponent of pi is exactly 2, a Roth-type exponent statement for the transcendental number pi that is neither effective nor about algebraic numbers.

Record asks a polynomial-time quantum algorithm for the dihedral hidden subgroup problem. Family 279 gives a polynomial-time uniform quantum circuit family that factors every integer exactly with probability one using a fixed gate set; both are quantum algorithms for number-theoretic hidden-structure problems, but neither settles the dihedral case.

Record is the Breuil-Mezard equality of Galois and automorphic sides for mod p representations. Family 010 proves pro-modularity at the prime two and Fontaine-Mazur modularity for 2-adic representations of G_Q, a neighbouring Hecke-algebra and modularity result that does not address the Breuil-Mezard equality.

Record asks the planar Erdos distinct-distances bound Omega(n/sqrt(log n)). Family 166 proves at least c_d n^{2/d} distances in R^d for d>=3, the higher-dimensional version of the same conjecture, and gives no planar bound.

Family 167 proves that all but o(n) points of any planar n-set determine at least n^{1-eps} distances, which implies D(n) >= n^{1-eps}; this is weaker than the known Guth-Katz bound n/log n, so it neither settles nor improves the record's target.

Record asks whether nonempty adelic Brauer-Manin set implies rational points for genus>=2 curves over number fields. Family 019 proves the p-adic section conjecture and the global section conjecture for X_0(N) and X_1(N), a rational-points-on-curves result by a different method that does not address the Brauer-Manin question.

Record asks algorithmic decidability of zeros of linear recurrence sequences (Skolem problem). Family 004 proves that no algorithm decides rational zeros of integer polynomials (Hilbert's tenth problem over Q); both are zero-existence decision problems, but the objects differ.

Record is Parshin's conjecture that higher K-groups of smooth projective varieties over finite fields are torsion. Family 209 disproves integral Gersten injectivity for two-dimensional ramified regular local rings, a K-theory result in the same area that does not address torsion over finite fields.

Record asks uniqueness of strongly rational holomorphic VOAs of central charge 24 with V_1=0 (moonshine uniqueness). Family 280 proves that every simple unitary strongly rational VOA generates a completely rational conformal net, the same class of objects but no uniqueness or central charge 24 result.

Record asks exact weighted all-pairs shortest paths in O(n^{3-eps}). Family 107 improves the matrix multiplication exponent omega to at most 9/4; fast matrix multiplication is the usual companion of APSP, but the family gives no min-plus or weighted APSP improvement.

Record asks whether every separable nuclear C*-algebra satisfies the UCT. Family 301 classifies separable nuclear C*-algebras after Razak-Jacelon stabilization via trace cones, which is the same nuclear classification area but says nothing about the UCT.

Record asks poly-time distribution-free PAC learning of DNF formulas. Family 127 proves average sensitivity at most 8d sqrt(n) for degree-d polynomial threshold functions, a Boolean-function tool from learning theory that does not yield a DNF learner.

Record asks equidistribution of Galois orbits of special points on Shimura varieties. Family 016 proves the abelian Zilber-Pink conjecture and a curve case in A_2, which concern special subvarieties but not equidistribution.

Record is Vaught's conjecture on the number of countable models of a complete countable theory. Family 240 proves Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture for abstract elementary classes, a neighbouring model-theoretic result with no bearing on counting countable models.

Record is the Hopf conjecture (nonnegative sectional curvature implies nonnegative Euler characteristic in even dimensions). Family 348 classifies Einstein four-manifolds with positive Einstein constant and nonnegative curvature by their universal covers, a neighbouring curvature classification that does not address Euler characteristic.

Record is Kawamata's conjecture that K-equivalence implies derived equivalence. Family 054 concerns derived-category equivalences of Kuznetsov components of cubic fourfolds, the same derived-category area, but it does not treat K-equivalent birational varieties.

Record asks closed aspherical manifold realizations of PD groups. Family 320 constructs homotopy-equivalent but non-homeomorphic closed aspherical four-manifolds with a common hyperbolic fundamental group, the same aspherical four-manifold setting but not a realization result.

Record concerns the Berry random-wave law for eigenfunctions on negatively curved manifolds. Family 350 studies nodal lengths and upper bounds for Laplace eigenfunctions (Yau's nodal bounds), an eigenfunction-geometry neighbour that gives no random-wave law.

Record asks freeness of the absolute Galois group of Q^ab. Family 031 proves Uchida's conjecture for open homomorphisms between absolute Galois groups of number fields, a structural result about Galois groups that does not decide freeness.

Family 325 proves the complete Crouzeix inequality with constant 2, whose second version is framed through optimal similarity; it is an operator-theoretic neighbour of Kadison similarity but does not settle similarity to *-representations (family 288 does).

Record asks whether a Banach space whose linear isometry group is transitive on its unit sphere is Hilbert. Family 322 solves Tingley's problem (surjective isometries between unit spheres extend to linear isometries), a neighbouring sphere-isometry result that does not address transitivity.

Record asks a uniform bound for surjectivity of mod-p Galois representations of non-CM elliptic curves over Q. Family 030 proves modularity of elliptic curves over imaginary quadratic fields, a neighbouring result about Galois representations of elliptic curves that gives no uniformity.

Record asks a deterministic k-competitive k-server algorithm for general metrics. Family 110 gives a randomized O(log^2(k+1)) competitive ratio on every metric, the same problem family with a different ratio and a randomized policy.

Record asks deterministic NC search for perfect matchings in general graphs. Family 113 gives an FPRAS for counting perfect matchings and proves the Anari-Oveis Gharan-Vinzant entropy conjecture; the same objects, but counting rather than NC search.

Record asks a deterministic NC algorithm for perfect matching search. Family 120 gives a randomized almost-linear-time maximum matching algorithm in general graphs, a sequential matching result in the same area.

Record is RL versus L. Family 137 gives a two-fifths-power space simulation of one-tape deterministic machines, a space-complexity simulation result in the same area that does not address randomized logspace.

Record asks holomorphic convexity of universal covers of smooth projective varieties. Family 058 (Kollar-Pardon) classifies semialgebraic universal covers of normal projective varieties, the same universal-cover setting without any holomorphic convexity conclusion.

Record asks rational polyhedral fundamental domains for the Morrison-Kawamata cone actions. Family 036 proves numerical semiampleness of nef adjoint classes and minimal models in numerical dimension one, MMP tools of the same area that do not address cone fundamental domains.

Record is Michel's boundary rigidity (boundary distance data determines the metric for simple manifolds). Family 344 proves the metric Blaschke theorem (injectivity radius equal to diameter forces a rank-one symmetric space), another metric-rigidity result from distance and geodesic data without boundary rigidity.

Record asks whether SDP feasibility is poly-time decidable in the Turing bit model. Family 126 proves exponential semidefinite lift size for the perfect matching polytope via PSD-rank bounds, the same SDP-complexity area but not a feasibility algorithm.

Record asks SDP feasibility complexity. Family 095 shows some hyperbolicity cones admit no finite affine semidefinite lift (refuting the projected Lax conjecture), a semidefinite-representability result rather than a feasibility algorithm.

Record asks whether MAJORITY is outside nonuniform ACC0. Family 112 constructs a polynomial-time language needing 2^{omega(sqrt n)} gates in depth-three OR-AND-OR circuits, a circuit lower bound in the same area but for a different class and function.

Record asks whether MAJORITY is outside ACC0. Family 274 proves parity is not computed by constant-depth quantum circuits (QAC0) with any fixed advantage, a circuit lower bound for a neighbouring class and function.

Record is the Cartan-Hadamard isoperimetric conjecture (nonpositive curvature). Family 354 determines the isoperimetric profile and minimizers of the flat cubic three-torus, a different isoperimetric problem in a compact flat space.

Record asks global regularity versus finite-time singularity for the 2D inviscid Boussinesq equations. Family 371 proves stable self-similar finite-time blowup for a defocusing nonlinear Schrodinger equation on a torus, the same question type for a different nonlinear evolution equation.

Record asks whether NPT bound entanglement exists (entangled, NPT, undistillable under LOCC). Family 272 constructs entangled states with zero distillable secret key, another distillability obstruction, but it does not address NPT states or LOCC entanglement distillation.
Record asks whether QMA(2)=QMA. Family 275 proves QMA-hardness of approximating continuum Coulomb energy, a QMA-type hardness result for a different problem that does not compare QMA with QMA(2).

Record is the Mahler volume-product bound. Family 091 proves the logarithmic Brunn-Minkowski conjecture for origin-symmetric convex bodies, a related convex-geometry inequality that does not itself give the Mahler bound.

Record is the Frey-Mazur conjecture (isomorphic p-torsion Galois modules force isogeny over Q for p>17). Family 030 proves modularity of elliptic curves over imaginary quadratic fields, a neighbouring elliptic-curve Galois-representation result over a different base field that does not address isogeny.

Record asks the growth of 3-uniform hypergraph Ramsey numbers. Family 160 gives superexponential lower bounds for van der Waerden numbers, a growth-rate result in Ramsey theory but for arithmetic progressions in colourings of the integers, not hypergraphs.

Record asks growth of 3-uniform hypergraph Ramsey numbers. Family 170 determines sharp logarithmic exponents of off-diagonal two-colour graph Ramsey numbers, a neighbouring Ramsey result for graphs rather than 3-uniform hypergraphs.

Record asks irrationality of Euler's constant gamma. Family 005 proves irrationality of Catalan's constant, a similar irrationality question for a different classical constant with a different argument.

Record asks the exponent chi for the passage-time variance in planar first-passage percolation. Family 212 proves absence of bigeodesics and strict convexity of the exponential limit shape in the same planar model, without any variance exponent.

Record is Asser's finite spectrum complement problem (spectra of first-order sentences over finite structures). Family 243 separates choiceless polynomial time with counting from polynomial time on unordered finite structures, a neighbouring finite-model-theory separation.

Record asks the exact unassisted quantum capacity of the qubit depolarizing channel. Family 276 determines the unassisted classical capacity of the generalized amplitude-damping channel, a neighbouring capacity result for a different channel and a different capacity.

Record asks explicit polynomial-time construction of graphs with clique and independence numbers O(log N). Family 178 gives a deterministic polynomial-time construction of explicit d-regular Ramanujan graphs, an explicit-graph construction of the same flavour but for expanders, not Ramsey graphs.

Record is Grigorchuk's gap conjecture (growth below exp(sqrt n) forces polynomial growth). Family 255 proves quasi-isometric recognition of virtually polycyclic groups, a related growth-classification theorem that does not give the gap.

Record is Komlos's conjecture (universal bound on signed sums of unit vectors in the infinity norm). Family 097 proves the Euclidean Steinitz-Bergstrom bound: signs keep every partial sum of unit vectors within C sqrt(d) in the Euclidean norm, the same signing area with a different norm and sum structure.

Record is the Alperin-McKay conjecture (equal numbers of height-zero characters in a block and its Brauer correspondent). Family 202 proves the blockwise Alperin weight count, a neighbouring local-global block-counting conjecture that does not address heights or McKay counts.

Record asks Montgomery's large-value bound for Dirichlet polynomials. Family 003 proves a zero-free half-plane for Dirichlet L-functions, the same analytic toolkit area without any large-value estimate.

Record asks that generic mean-curvature-flow singularities are modeled on spheres or cylinders. Family 355 proves uniqueness of tangent flows at the first singular time of surface mean-curvature flow in R^3, the same singularity-theory area with no generic classification.

Record is Huisken's generic singularity conjecture for mean-curvature flow. Family 351 proves Ricci-flow extension past finite times with bounded scalar curvature on closed four-manifolds, a singularity result for a different flow.

Record is the Bass-Quillen conjecture (projective modules over polynomial rings over regular rings are extended). Family 209 disproves integral Gersten injectivity for ramified regular local rings, a K-theory result over regular rings that does not address projective modules.

Record asks small-time global exact null controllability of Navier-Stokes by boundary data. Family 376 constructs smooth external forcings steering incompressible viscous flows on a flat three-torus through universal computation, the same forced/controlled fluid setting but no boundary null controllability.

Record asks whether every one-ended hyperbolic group contains a closed surface group. Family 246 proves Cannon's conjecture (hyperbolic groups with S^2 boundary act on hyperbolic 3-space), a neighbouring hyperbolic-group result with no surface subgroup conclusion.

Record asks surface subgroups in one-ended hyperbolic groups. Family 257 constructs a hyperbolic group with a finite classifying space and no geometric CAT(0) action, a hyperbolic-group counterexample that does not address surface subgroups.

Record asks surface subgroups in one-ended hyperbolic groups. Family 258 proves that word-hyperbolic one-relator groups are virtually compact special (and Gersten's conjecture), hyperbolic-group structure results that do not produce surface subgroups.

Record is the Vassiliev separation of knots by abelian-valued finite-type invariants. Family 306 proves the purely cosmetic surgery conjecture for knots in S^3, a different knot-theoretic problem about Dehn surgery.

Record is the normality of pi (equal digit-block frequencies in every base). Family 017 proves the irrationality exponent of pi is 2, a statement about rational approximation to pi; irrationality exponents do not imply normality.

Record asks whether randomized communication complexity of total functions is polynomially bounded by quantum communication complexity. Family 284 gives the optimal quartic separation R(f)=O((1+Q(f))^4) in the query model, the same randomized-versus-quantum comparison but not in the communication model.
Record asks for the exact real Grothendieck constant K_G (Krivine-Grothendieck inequality). Family 312 is the Grothendieck homotopy hypothesis for infinity-groupoids, sharing only the eponym.

Record asks for a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm deciding perfect matchings with exactly k red edges. Family 120 gives a randomized almost-linear-time algorithm for maximum-cardinality matching in general graphs, which shares the 'exact matching' name only.

Record is Dixmier's conjecture that every endomorphism of the first Weyl algebra over a characteristic-zero field is an automorphism. Family 251 solves Dixmier's unitarizability problem for discrete groups, a different problem with the same eponym.

Record asks L(1/2, chi) nonzero for every primitive Dirichlet character. Family 007 proves Chowla's two-point correlation conjecture for Liouville-type multiplicative functions, a different Chowla conjecture.
Record is Zariski's multiplicity conjecture for hypersurface germs. Family 047 concerns Zariski cancellation for affine fourfolds, a different Zariski problem.
Record is Zariski's multiplicity conjecture. Family 048 is the Lipman-Zariski conjecture on the tangent sheaf of normal affine surfaces, a different Zariski problem.

Record asks for Hadamard matrices of every order 4k. Family 179 proves the circulant Hadamard conjecture (real circulant Hadamard matrices exist only in orders 1 and 4), a restricted-structure question that does not bear on general Hadamard existence.

Record asks that every lattice in PU(n,1), n >= 4, be arithmetic. Family 286 classifies bimodules and proves arithmetic exhaustion for von Neumann algebras of lattice group factors, a different notion of arithmeticity.

Record asks for the order of ex(n, C_2k), the Turán number of an even cycle. Family 165 settles the Harary-Hill and Zarankiewicz crossing numbers and Turán's brickyard problem, which concerns crossing numbers, not Turán numbers.
Record asks whether the Turán density of K_4^(3) is 5/9. Family 165 is about planar crossing numbers (Turán's brickyard problem), not hypergraph Turán density.
Record asks whether every one-relation monoid has a solvable word problem. Family 258 concerns one-relator groups (Gersten's conjecture and hyperbolicity), a related but different algebraic class.
Record is Mazur's conjecture on the real topology of rational points. Family 010 is the Fontaine-Mazur modularity result at the prime two, sharing the eponym only.
Record is Gromov's filling area conjecture for orientable surfaces. Family 335 is Gromov's integral scalar-curvature bound for simplicial volume, a different Gromov conjecture.
Record is Hilbert's third problem on scissors congruence. Family 143 is Hilbert's sixteenth problem on limit-cycle bounds, a different Hilbert problem.
Record is Hilbert's third problem. Family 304 is the Hilbert-Smith conjecture on group actions on manifolds, a different Hilbert conjecture.
Record is Margulis's bounded diagonal-orbit conjecture for SL(3,R)/SL(3,Z). Family 018 is the Margulis-Platonov normal-subgroup conjecture over global fields, a different Margulis conjecture.
Record is Shelah's conjecture on NIP fields in model theory. Family 240 is Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture for abstract elementary classes, a different Shelah conjecture.
Record is Green's canonical syzygy conjecture on K_{p,1}(C,K_C). Family 200 is the Eisenbud-Green-Harris conjecture on Hilbert functions and lex-plus-powers ideals, a different Green conjecture.

Record asks whether every point of the closed discontinuity set of a reduced homogeneous (lambda=0) planar Mumford-Shah minimizer has a C^1 normal form (diameter, one radius, or three radii at 120 degrees). Family 366 proves interior regularity (C^{1,alpha} arc, crack tip, or three arcs at 120 degrees) for reduced minimizers with bounded fidelity data, a different energy with a fidelity term; the reviewer should check whether that argument also covers the homogeneous case.

Record is the marked length spectrum rigidity conjecture for negatively curved metrics. Family 339 proves Katok's entropy rigidity (Liouville measure maximizes geodesic-flow entropy iff the metric is locally symmetric) in the same negative-curvature setting, a related rigidity statement that does not address length spectra.

Record asks for a positive liminf of the staggered-magnetization squared expectation for the 2D spin-1/2 square-lattice Heisenberg antiferromagnet. Family 271 proves Bloch's law and spontaneous magnetization for 3D quantum Heisenberg ferromagnets, the same model family in another dimension and sign regime, with no statement on the 2D antiferromagnet.

Record is Neel order for the 2D spin-1/2 square-lattice Heisenberg antiferromagnet. Family 268 proves the spin-one Haldane gap for 1D antiferromagnetic chains, a different dimension, spin and property.

Record asks for L(1/2,chi) nonzero and explicitly excludes off-central zero-free regions. Family 003 proves zero-free half-planes Re s > 7/8 (and 11/12) and uniform exclusion of real Landau-Siegel zeros near 1; these do not reach the central point 1/2, so the link is only that both concern zeros of Dirichlet L-functions.

Record asks for integrality of L2-Betti numbers of universal covers of torsion-free groups (Atiyah). Family 315 proves the four-dimensional Singer conjecture (L2-Betti numbers of aspherical four-manifolds vanish outside degree two); same L2-invariant setting, but nothing on integrality.

Record asks whether multiplicity is an invariant of embedded topological type of hypersurface germs. Family 064 proves topological right-triviality for one-parameter families of isolated surface singularities with constant Milnor number (the mu-constant problem), a topological-classification result that does not compare multiplicities.

Record is Broue's conjecture (derived equivalence of a block with abelian defect group and its Brauer correspondent). Family 202 proves the numerical blockwise Alperin weight conjecture (simple modules equal weight classes), a numerical invariant that a derived equivalence would preserve; no derived equivalence is established.

Record is Broue's abelian defect group conjecture. Family 203 proves Donovan's finiteness conjecture (finitely many Morita classes of blocks with bounded defect order), a related block-theoretic finiteness result that gives no derived equivalences.

Record asks for Calderon uniqueness for bounded measurable scalar conductivities. Family 372 proves global uniqueness for smooth isotropic elasticity (Lame moduli) from the full displacement-to-traction map, a smooth vector-valued analogue that does not address bounded measurable scalar conductivities.

Record asks that the nearest-neighbour q-state Potts transition on Z^d (d >= 3, q >= 3) be first order. Family 228 constructs stable continuum pair potentials in 3D with a first-order phase transition, a different model with the same phenomenon type.

Record asks for a first-order Potts transition on Z^d for d >= 3. Family 223 proves SLE_kappa limits for critical square-lattice random-cluster (Potts-type) interfaces, a two-dimensional critical result.
Record concerns the Potts transition for d >= 3. Family 233 identifies the joint scaling limit of critical Ashkin-Teller currents, including the four-state Potts endpoint, in two dimensions.

Record is the Cerny conjecture on reset words of synchronizing DFAs. Family 129 proves exponential state lower bounds for two-way automata (complementation and simulation), a different automata-complexity question in the same area.

Record is the Hadamard matrix existence conjecture for every order 4k. Family 266 proves N(6)=3 for mutually unbiased bases and Fourier vanishing for order-six complex Hadamard matrices, a different (complex, order-six) Hadamard question.
Record asks for irrationality of zeta(5). Family 005 proves irrationality of Catalan's constant, a different special value in a similar series-irrationality setting, with no zeta(5) content.

Record is nonlinear Landau damping for Vlasov-Poisson at the Gevrey threshold. Family 362 proves large-data global existence and uniqueness for relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell, a different kinetic-field system with no Landau damping claim.

Record asks for a positive combinatorial rule for all Kronecker coefficients. Family 205 proves Saxl's conjecture (the tensor square of each staircase representation contains every irreducible), a positivity statement for one family of Kronecker coefficients with no rule.

Record asks for the exact average-error capacity of the binary deletion channel. Family 122 gives trace-reconstruction sample bounds for the same deletion channel, a different quantity with no capacity result.

Record is Bott's conjecture that nonnegatively curved simply connected manifolds are rationally elliptic. Family 348 classifies closed nonnegatively curved Einstein four-manifolds (S^4, CP^2, S^2 x S^2) under an L2 gap, a four-dimensional curvature classification that does not address rational ellipticity.

Record asks for the L^p operator norm of the Beurling-Ahlfors transform (Iwaniec). Family 083 proves uniform L2 bounds for planar Hilbert transforms along Lipschitz unit vector fields at short scale, a related planar singular-integral result with no norm bound for the Beurling-Ahlfors transform.

Record is Brauer's conjecture k(B) <= |D| on ordinary characters of blocks. Family 202 proves the numerical blockwise Alperin weight count (simple Brauer characters versus weights), a different block invariant with no bound on k(B).
Record concerns k(B) for blocks with defect group D. Family 203 proves Donovan's finiteness theorem for blocks of bounded defect order, a related block-theory result that does not bound k(B).

Record asks p_c < p_u on non-amenable Cayley graphs. Family 213 proves that at the critical probability there is no infinite cluster on every infinite quasi-transitive graph with p_c < 1 (Benjamini-Schramm criticality), a different threshold statement on the same graph class.

Record is the congruence subgroup property for Mod(S), genus at least three. Family 252 constructs a torsion-free word-hyperbolic group that is not residually finite, refuting the assumption that all word-hyperbolic groups are residually finite, which the record's status says the Wilton-Sisto conditional theorem uses; it does not settle the congruence subgroup property.

Record is the Thomson problem (minimal Coulomb energy of N points on S^2 for each N). Family 090 proves planar triangular-lattice optimality for energies and the linear term of optimal spherical logarithmic energy, asymptotic and planar results rather than minimizers for each N.

Record is Ivrii's conjecture that periodic billiard orbits have measure zero in any bounded smooth domain. Family 147 concerns billiards whose boundary is an ellipse under invariant-curve foliations, the same billiard map in a rigidity setting that does not address the measure of periodic orbits.

Record asks about the measure of periodic billiard orbits. Family 150 proves ergodicity (and weak mixing) of billiard flows in triangles with an irrational angle, a different billiard-dynamics result.

Record is Clemens's conjecture on finitely many rational curves of each degree on a general quintic threefold. Family 055 proves Toda's Gepner conjecture by constructing a stability condition on every smooth quintic threefold, the same object with no statement about rational curves.

Record is Whitehead's asphericity question for subcomplexes of aspherical 2-complexes. Family 321 disproves Wall's finite D(2) problem with a finite 3-complex lacking a 2-dimensional homotopy model, a neighbouring finiteness question about 2-complexes with no asphericity content.
Record is Whitehead asphericity. Family 254 proves the Artin K(pi,1) conjecture (Salvetti complexes are aspherical), an asphericity result for specific complexes that does not address subcomplexes.

Record asks that a hyperbolic compact Kahler manifold have ample canonical bundle. Family 068 proves that if -K_X is smoothly semipositive then H^0(X,-mK_X) is nonzero for some m, a canonical-bundle positivity statement in another direction.

Record asks for global regularity of large-data 3D incompressible Hall-MHD. Family 376 constructs forced Navier-Stokes flows that perform universal computation, a different incompressible-fluid question with no regularity claim.

Record is Polya's eigenvalue bound for Dirichlet Laplacians on bounded domains. Family 262 gives sharp one-dimensional matrix Lieb-Thirring inequalities (sums of negative eigenvalue moments of Schrodinger operators), a related spectral-bound theme on a different operator.

Record is Polya's conjecture for Dirichlet eigenvalues. Family 369 proves a strict hot-spots statement for Neumann eigenfunctions on simply connected planar domains, a related spectral-geometry result for a different boundary problem.

Record asks for the sharp three-dimensional Lieb-Thirring constant L_{1,3} = 1/(15 pi^2). Family 262 determines the sharp one-dimensional matrix Lieb-Thirring constant for 1/2 < gamma < 3/2 with all equality cases; a different dimension and exponent, with no 3D constant.

Record is the Arnold-Givental bound on real-Lagrangian intersections for Hamiltonian images. Family 347 disproves stable-Morse and strong Arnold fixed-point bounds (a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of the quadric threefold with exactly three fixed points), the same Arnold-type counting theme for fixed points rather than Lagrangian intersections.

Record concerns intersections of real Lagrangians with Hamiltonian images. Family 340 disproves the nearby Lagrangian conjecture (an exact embedded Lagrangian diffeomorphic to the base but not Hamiltonian isotopic to the zero section), the same Lagrangian topology area with a different claim.

Record is Pugh-Shub C^r density of stable ergodicity among partially hyperbolic volume-preserving diffeomorphisms. Family 144 gives a smooth volume-preserving diffeomorphism of the three-torus with simple Lebesgue spectrum, a smooth ergodic-theory result with no stable-ergodicity density claim.

Record is stable ergodicity in partial hyperbolicity. Family 146 proves positive metric entropy for the standard sine map at large parameters, a different smooth-ergodic result for an explicit family, not a stable-ergodicity density statement.

Record asks whether every finite coloring of the positive integers has a monochromatic solution of x^2 + y^2 = z^2. Family 164 proves Hindman's finite sums and products theorem (monochromatic subset sums and products), a partition-regularity result for different configurations.

Record is partition regularity of Pythagorean triples. Family 160 gives superexponential bounds for van der Waerden numbers (monochromatic arithmetic progressions), another Ramsey-type quantity with no Pythagorean content.

Record asks for a global smooth cubic defocusing NLS solution on T^2 with unbounded H^s norm (Bourgain). Family 371 proves stable finite-time blowup for a supercritical defocusing NLS on T^12 with large odd power, the same equation type on a torus but finite-time blowup in another dimension and nonlinearity, not infinite-time Sobolev growth.

Record asks that nef isotropic line bundles on IHS manifolds be semiample. Family 036 proves numerical semiampleness of nef adjoint classes for klt pairs and smooth compact Kahler pairs, a semiampleness result for other bundle classes.

Record is Martin's conjecture on Turing-invariant functions under AD. Family 241 proves that every order automorphism of the Turing degrees is the identity, a related structural fact about the same degree structure that does not address Turing-invariant functions.

Record is Legendre's conjecture (a prime between consecutive squares), which would bound prime gaps from above. Family 026 proves a positive proportion of prime gaps exceed C log p, a large-gap result in the opposite regime.

Record asks for deterministic decision of perfect matchings with exactly k red edges. Family 113 gives a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for counting perfect matchings with exact zero detection, a counting problem on the same objects with no exact-k decision.

Record is Jones's unknot conjecture (Jones polynomial detects the unknot). Family 306 proves the purely cosmetic surgery conjecture for knots in S^3, a knot-theory result on Dehn surgery slopes with no Jones-polynomial content.
Record asks for a polynomial-time unknot recognition algorithm. Family 306 concerns Dehn surgery slopes on knots, a different knot-theoretic question with no algorithmic content.

Record is the log-Brunn-Minkowski inequality for symmetric convex bodies. Family 087 proves the symmetric Mahler volume-product bound |K||K polar| >= 4^n/n! with equality cases, a related convex-geometry volume inequality from the same symmetric-body circle, not log-BM.

Record is log-Brunn-Minkowski. Family 088 proves Petty's projection-volume conjecture (ellipsoids minimize projection-body volume) and the Lutwak-Petty projection inequalities, the same Lutwak-school convex-geometry area with a different functional.

Record is Koebe's circle-domain uniformization for domains in the Riemann sphere. Family 072 proves Brennan's conjecture (integrability of |phi'|^s for conformal maps) and sharp integral-means bounds for univalent maps, a related conformal-mapping question with no circle-domain content.

Record is Serre's positivity of intersection multiplicities. Family 194 proves Lech's multiplicity conjecture (e(R) <= e(S) for flat local homomorphisms), a related multiplicity inequality in commutative algebra.

Record is strict comparison implies Z-stability. Family 299 proves the Kirchberg-Rordam character criterion (Z-absorption iff the central-sequence algebra has no characters), a different Z-stability characterization that does not use comparison.

Record is the Toms-Winter problem for simple nuclear algebras. Family 301 classifies separable nuclear algebras after tensoring with the Razak-Jacelon algebra via trace cones, a classification result in the same Jiang-Su circle that does not use strict comparison.
Record is Toms-Winter. Family 303 proves that properly infinite positive elements give strong pure infiniteness and Cuntz absorption, a related absorption theorem that does not involve comparison.

Record asks whether bounded diagonal orbits in SL(3,R)/SL(3,Z) are closed (Margulis). Family 015 proves Haar equidistribution without escape of mass for torus packets over totally real fields, a homogeneous-dynamics result on arithmetic quotients with a different orbit family and no closedness claim.

Record is arithmeticity of lattices in PU(n,1), n >= 4. Family 018 proves the Margulis-Platonov normal-subgroup conjecture over global fields, a neighbouring arithmetic-group result about normal subgroups, not lattice arithmeticity.

Record is the original Dubrovin conjecture linking semisimple quantum cohomology and full exceptional collections for Fano manifolds. Family 063 proves the generalized Mukai inequality rho(iota-1) <= n for Fano manifolds, the same class of objects with a different invariant and no quantum-cohomology or exceptional-collection content.

Record asks for NP-hardness of a constant-factor approximation for Densest k-Subgraph. Family 102 proves the Unique Games Conjecture and direct NP-hardness of approximation thresholds for Max-Cut, Vertex Cover, Min-UnCut and directed feedback vertex set, the standard hardness toolkit but no DkS result.

Record is DkS approximation hardness. Family 117 proves NP-hardness of constant-factor approximation for Uniform Sparsest Cut and Goemans-Linial integrality gaps, a different graph-partition hardness result.

Record is Freyd's generating hypothesis for maps between finite spectra. Family 316 proves Curtis's conjecture on the mod-two stable Hurewicz image of spheres, a stable-homotopy result about spheres with no statement on maps between finite spectra.

Record asks for exact kissing numbers in dimensions n > 4. Family 090 proves planar circle-packing optimality (the Cohn-Elkies sharpness) and triangular-lattice energy minimality, a planar packing and energy result with no higher-dimensional kissing content.

Record is Gromov's filling area conjecture for surfaces with boundary a circle of length 2 pi. Family 337 proves sharp isoperimetry for curvature at most 0 and sharp Euclidean integral filling in CAT(0) spaces, a related filling and isoperimetry theme with no surface-area bound.

Record asks about k-fold correlation convergence for one mixing transformation. Family 154 proves almost-everywhere convergence of consecutive multiple ergodic averages for invertible mixing transformations with no mixing rate; it uses mixing but does not address the correlation question.

Record asks for the sharp isotropic-constant bound (simplex). Family 091 proves the logarithmic Brunn-Minkowski inequality for origin-symmetric convex bodies and the B-conjecture for log-concave measures, neighboring volume inequalities that do not bound the isotropic constant L_K.

Record asks whether the first nonzero eigenvalue of every closed embedded minimal hypersurface of S^{n+1} equals n. Family 349 proves the Solomon-Yau least-volume conjecture for minimal hypersurfaces of round spheres (volume bounded below by minimal Clifford products); same objects, different invariant.

Family 350 is titled Yau's nodal bounds: it proves the sharp C sqrt(lambda) nodal-length bound for Laplace eigenfunctions on fixed smooth surfaces. This is a different Yau conjecture about eigenfunction nodal sets, not the first eigenvalue of minimal hypersurfaces.

Family 361 disproves Yau's proposed Euclidean dimension bound for harmonic functions of integer growth on manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature. Another Yau conjecture, about harmonic functions rather than the first eigenvalue of minimal hypersurfaces.

Record asks for the least n such that undecidability holds for integer polynomials in at most n variables over Z. Family 004 proves Hilbert's tenth problem over Q is undecidable for arbitrarily many variables; a neighboring undecidability result over a different ring, with no variable count over Z.

Family 242 proves every r.e. set has a single-fold Diophantine representation and that Diophantine solvability over the naturals stays undecidable under an at-most-one-solution promise. This is Diophantine undecidability near the record, but it gives no variable count for integer polynomials over Z.

Family 119 proves the Courtade-Kumar conjecture on the information a Boolean function retains after independent bit-flip noise. It is an entropy-type statement about Boolean functions, but about mutual information under noise rather than spectral entropy versus influence.

Record asks whether spectral entropy of a Boolean function is at most C times its total influence. Family 127 bounds the average sensitivity (total influence) of degree-d polynomial threshold functions by 8d sqrt(n); it bounds an influence quantity but says nothing about spectral entropy.

The record's Fourier entropy-influence conjecture is attributed to Friedgut and Kalai; family 186 proves the Friedgut-Kalai threshold-width conjectures for graph and hypergraph properties. Same name, different problem: it says nothing about spectral entropy versus total influence.

Family 165 is the Zarankiewicz crossing-number problem (Harary-Hill and Zarankiewicz crossing formulas). The record is the extremal Zarankiewicz problem for ex(n, K_{t,t}); same name, different problem.

Record asks for eventual exclusion of positive-dimensional special subvarieties of A_g generically contained in the smooth Torelli locus, for g large. Family 016 proves the abelian Zilber-Pink conjecture and the Zilber-Pink curve case in A_2; Zilber-Pink is the umbrella for such exclusions, but neither the large-genus Torelli statement nor the A_2 curve case is the record's target.

Record asks for the valid scope of Bartnik's quasi-local mass conjectures via asymptotically flat static vacuum extensions. Family 260 proves an enclosing-area spacetime Penrose inequality bounding ADM mass below; a neighboring mass inequality, not a characterization of static extensions.

Record asks for Colmez's formula for the stable Faltings height of CM abelian varieties. Family 032 proves the rational Hodge conjecture for every complex CM abelian variety; same objects (CM abelian varieties), different question.

Record asks whether, for finite fundamental groups, positive scalar curvature is equivalent to vanishing of the real Rosenberg index. Family 335 proves Gromov's integral scalar-curvature inequality and rational inessentiality under positive scalar curvature; a neighboring psc obstruction that does not establish the finite-group equivalence (its 'Gromov-Lawson conjecture' is a different statement).

Record concerns flow-cut gaps for minor-closed families. Family 117 proves NP-hardness of Uniform Sparsest Cut and sqrt(log n)-type integrality gaps for the Goemans-Linial relaxation on general graphs with unit demands; same flow-cut-gap area, but no minor-closed statement.

Record is the Zariski cancellation problem. Family 049 disproves the stable-coordinate conjecture in four variables (a polynomial that becomes a coordinate only after adjoining a variable), a closely related coordinate-stabilization statement but not the cancellation claim.

Bernoulli convolutions are self-similar measures. Family 148 proves dim_H mu = min{1, h_RW/chi} for every finite self-similar measure on the line; this is a dimension formula and does not decide absolute continuity of nu_lambda.

Record asks for uniform epsilon-equilibria in finite multiplayer stochastic games with average payoffs. Family 104 gives quasipolynomial algorithms for two-player turn-based stochastic mean-payoff games and mean-payoff parity games; same game class, but it computes zero-sum values and strategies, not equilibria.

Record asks for uniqueness of tangent cones of area-minimizing integral currents in codimension at least two. Family 346 bounds the singular set of stationary integral varifolds by Hausdorff dimension m-1; a regularity neighbor that does not address uniqueness of blow-up limits.

Record asks for a constant-competitive online rule when elements arrive in uniformly random order against adversarial weights (matroid secretary). Family 111 gives a one-sample matroid prophet inequality against an adversarial arrival order with independent random values; same matroid online-selection area but a different model.
Family 196 disproves Kaplansky's zero-divisor conjecture (F_2[G] has zero divisors for a torsion-free finitely presented G); a different Kaplansky conjecture from direct finiteness.
Family 207 proves the l^1-Bass conjecture and, algebraically, Kaplansky's idempotent conjecture for torsion-free groups; other Kaplansky group-ring conjectures, not direct finiteness.
Family 285 disproves the Kadison-Kaplansky conjecture (no nontrivial projections in the reduced group C*-algebra of a torsion-free group); a different conjecture carrying Kaplansky's name.
Record is Minkowski's conjecture on products of non-homogeneous linear forms; family 091 proves Brunn-Minkowski-type inequalities for convex bodies. Same name, different problem.

Record asks whether R detecting the n-th Greek-letter family forces K(R) to detect the (n+1)-st. Family 311 proves Chai's invariant-ideal conjecture and the Hovey-Strickland thick-ideal conjecture for dualizable K(n)-local spectra; a chromatic-homotopy neighbor that does not treat Greek-letter detection by K-theory.
Family 313 proves every homotopy group of the K(n)-local sphere is a finitely generated Z_p-module; a chromatic neighbor on the K(n)-local side of the redshift question, not the redshift implication.

Family 319 disproves the Hahn-Wilson finite-generation conjecture at chromatic height two; this sits in the same finite-generation and redshift circle for BP<n>-type spectra but does not address Greek-letter detection.

Record asks whether every nonamenable II_1 factor contains L(F_2). Family 287 proves L(F_2) and L(F_3) are isomorphic, hence all interpolated free group factors are isomorphic; a free-group-factor neighbor that does not address containment of L(F_2) in nonamenable factors.

Family 082 proves a symmetric L^3 x L^3 -> L^{3/2} maximal estimate for the planar triangular Hilbert transform, a bilinear operator on R^2. It is a different operator from the record's one-dimensional trilinear form with slopes 1, 2, 3, and at a different exponent point.

Record asks whether K_X + (n+2)L is very ample. Family 038 proves Fujita's freeness conjecture (K_X + mL globally generated for m >= n+1), a companion Fujita statement at a weaker level; freeness does not give very ampleness.

Record asks whether every convex body can be illuminated by 2^n external sources. Family 156 disproves Borsuk's covering assertion in dimension nine via a compact set of rank-one projectors; the Borsuk and Hadwiger covering circle is related, but the 2^n illumination bound is not addressed.

Family 157 disproves Hadwiger's graph-coloring conjecture (chromatic number versus clique-minor order, even fractionally); the record is the Hadwiger-Boltyanski illumination conjecture. Same name, different problem.

Record is Kothe's conjecture on nil one-sided ideals. Family 247 constructs an infinite finitely presented residually finite 2-group and an infinite-dimensional finitely presented nil associative F_2-algebra; a nil-algebra neighbor, not the one-sided-ideal statement.

Record asks whether every balanced presentation of the trivial group is Andrews-Curtis trivial. Family 256 resolves Howie's conjecture on equations over groups and proves a Kervaire-type statement about adjoining one generator and one relation; both concern presentations, but neither addresses balanced presentations of the trivial group (a weak link).

Record asks for the maximum size of k-uniform families with no s pairwise disjoint members (Erdos matching). Family 162 disproves Ryser's covering conjecture for intersecting r-partite hypergraphs (covering number versus matching number); the same extremal intersection theory, but no bound on the Erdos matching quantity.

Record asks whether every free and rotund irreducible V in C^n x (C*)^n contains a point (z, exp z). Family 016 proves the abelian Zilber-Pink conjecture on atypical intersections with torsion cosets; the same atypical-intersection paradigm, but a different setting with no exponential points.

Record asks for a coordinate of large influence for low-degree polynomials. Family 127 bounds the average sensitivity (total influence) of degree-d threshold functions by 8d sqrt(n); a total-influence upper bound, not a lower bound on one coordinate's influence.

Record asks whether every degree-d polynomial f: {-1,1}^n -> [0,1] has a coordinate of influence at least poly(1/d, Var f). Family 192 disproves a square-root bound relating linear Fourier coefficients of Boolean functions to degree; a degree-versus-influence neighbor that does not treat the Aaronson-Ambainis statement.

Record asks for the decidability of the existential theory of C(t) with a named transcendental t. Family 004 proves Hilbert's tenth problem over Q is undecidable; a neighboring undecidability result over a different field, with C(t) not covered.

Record asks for a polynomial-time algorithm for Condon's simple stochastic (reachability) games. Family 104 gives deterministic quasipolynomial algorithms for turn-based stochastic mean-payoff games and mean-payoff parity games; a quasipolynomial, mean-payoff neighbor that does not claim polynomial time for simple stochastic games.

Record asks whether affine crystallographic groups are virtually solvable (Auslander), equivalently whether fundamental groups of compact complete affine manifolds are virtually polycyclic. Family 255 proves quasi-isometric recognition of virtually polycyclic groups; a neighbor about the same group class that does not address affine crystallographic groups.

Family 199 disproves the Auslander-Reiten homological conjecture (and Tachikawa's second conjecture) with finite-dimensional algebras; the record is the group-theoretic Auslander conjecture on affine crystallographic groups. Same name, different problem.

Record asks for the McKay-Navarro (Galois-McKay) counting. Family 202 proves the blockwise Alperin weight conjecture (counting Brauer characters by weights); a local-global block-counting neighbor with no Galois action.

Record asks whether lim R(k,k)^{1/k} exists. Family 170 gives r(s,t) = t^{s-1}/(log t)^{s-2+o(1)} for fixed s >= 5 as t grows (off-diagonal, s fixed); Ramsey asymptotics that do not bear on the diagonal limit.

Family 059 disproves Zariski's multiplicity conjecture (ambiently homeomorphic hypersurfaces with different multiplicities); a different Zariski conjecture from the locally-free-tangent-sheaf question.

Record is the SHGH specialness criterion (special iff the fixed locus contains a multiple (-1)-curve). Family 039 proves Nagata's strict inequality sum m_i < d sqrt(r) for r >= 10 very general points, a related plane linear-system result that is not the specialness criterion.

Record asks that irreducible unimodular Pisot substitution systems have pure discrete spectrum. Family 153 classifies singularity of Bernoulli convolutions and treats Pisot and Salem reciprocals; a Pisot-number neighbor with no substitution-spectrum statement.

Record asks for a polynomial-time algorithm producing N points on S^2 with log energy within c log N of the minimum. Family 090 proves triangular-lattice minimality and the Brauchart-Hardin-Saff linear-term conjecture for spherical logarithmic energy; it sharpens knowledge of the minimal energy but gives no construction or O(log N) error.

Family 016 proves Zilber-Pink finiteness for abelian varieties and curves in A_2; the record is Zilber's quasiminimality conjecture for the complex exponential field. Same surname, different conjecture.

Record asks whether induced-T-free graphs are chi-bounded for every tree T (Gyarfas-Sumner). Family 184 proves an Alon-Krivelevich-Sudakov coloring bound for graphs avoiding a fixed (not necessarily induced) subgraph and an Ajtai-Erdos-Komlos-Szemeredi independence bound; a neighbor on coloring with forbidden subgraphs, not chi-boundedness for induced trees.

Record asks whether every parallelohedron is an affine image of a Dirichlet-Voronoi polytope. Family 155 gives a finite translational tile in Z^3 that tiles space but admits no periodic tiling; a translational space-tiling neighbor, not the parallelohedron classification.

Record asks whether list chromatic index equals chromatic index for loopless multigraphs. Family 184 proves correspondence-coloring bounds (a generalization of list coloring) for vertex coloring of graphs avoiding a fixed subgraph; a list-coloring neighbor, not list edge-coloring.

Record asks for anticoncentration of the permanent of Gaussian matrices. Family 108 proves an Omega(n^3) lower bound on the border determinantal complexity of the permanent; a permanent-complexity neighbor with no distributional statement.

Record asks for potential density of rational points on K3 surfaces. Family 027 concerns potential Zariski density of integral points on SL_r character varieties of curves (Litt's integral-density question); the same potential-density paradigm for different objects and a different question.
